purpose: machine-readable expert-system KB for planning, evaluating, prioritizing, and validating archival appraisal and description work units (appraisal theory, provenance and original order, arrangement and description standards, accessioning and accruals, retention and disposition, lifecycle vs continuum, authenticity and chain of custody, digital records appraisal, and access/privacy) as a subdomain node of a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: subdomain of library, archival science and data curation; framed for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB
no observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors

covers appraisal theory, provenance/order, arrangement/description standards, accessioning/accruals, retention/disposition, lifecycle vs continuum, authenticity/custody, digital appraisal, and access/privacy
session-bounded work units suitable for heavy LLM-assisted execution and handoff
exclusions: physical conservation and preservation treatment (preservation subdomain)
repository/digital-preservation storage engineering and format migration execution
rights and copyright legal adjudication beyond capturing access/rights metadata
research-data curation pipelines beyond shared appraisal/description concepts

competency_questions.question: Which appraisal theory and records model govern selection decisions for this records body?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: APPRAISAL_THEORY and LIFECYCLE_VS_CONTINUUM present with selection rationale

competency_questions.question: What value criteria justify keeping or destroying a series, how are they reviewed, and how is the program governed for consistency and auditability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: APPRAISAL_DECISION and GOVERNANCE_QA define criteria application, peer review, and program audit

competency_questions.question: How does an appraisal decision flow into a defensible retention period and a controlled disposition action?
How are provenance (respect des fonds) and original order established before arrangement, including multiple or shifting provenance a single hierarchy cannot express?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVENANCE and ORIGINAL_ORDER precede ARRANGEMENT; RIC_MODELING handles multiprovenance

competency_questions.question: At what level of arrangement should this fonds be processed, and which DACS elements are required at each level?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ARRANGEMENT defines level-of-arrangement; DACS_DESCRIPTION defines element-by-level coverage

competency_questions.question: How is descriptive content encoded (EAD) and validated for machine-actionable discovery?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EAD_ENCODING depends on DACS_DESCRIPTION and outputs valid XML

competency_questions.question: How is description exchanged, crosswalked, and aggregated across repositories and standards?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTEROP_EXCHANGE, ISADG_CROSSWALK, and RIC_MODELING cover crosswalk and aggregation

competency_questions.question: What must an accession record capture to establish legal and physical custody?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCESSIONING outputs control number, extent, and rights statement

competency_questions.question: How are accruals integrated into an existing fonds without fragmenting provenance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCRUALS depends on ACCESSIONING and ARRANGEMENT

competency_questions.question: How are retention periods authorized and disposition executed with hold and audit controls?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETENTION_SCHEDULE cites authority; DISPOSITION gates on hold check and certificate

competency_questions.question: When are born-digital records appraised and captured given the lifecycle vs continuum model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIGITAL_APPRAISAL depends on LIFECYCLE_VS_CONTINUUM and APPRAISAL_THEORY

competency_questions.question: How are authenticity, integrity, and an unbroken chain of custody established and maintained, including during digital capture?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUTHENTICITY, CHAIN_OF_CUSTODY, and DIGITAL_APPRAISAL preserve integrity and custody evidence

competency_questions.question: How are access restrictions and privacy protections determined and documented?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCESS_RESTRICTIONS sets policy with legal/donor basis

competency_questions.question: How do access tools deliver description while enforcing restrictions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCESS_TOOLS depends on ACCESS_RESTRICTIONS and DACS_DESCRIPTION

glossary.definition: principle of keeping records of one creator together as a unit
the sequence and organization in which the creator kept the records
value of records to their original creator for ongoing business use
enduring value to researchers; evidential and informational value
function-based appraisal selecting records by the significance of the functions that created them
collaborative plan to document an area or activity across repositories
linear model of records from creation through active/inactive use to disposition
model treating recordkeeping as continuous overlapping dimensions, not linear stages
information about origin, custody, and chain of ownership of records
documented succession of custody and actions on records since creation
property that a record is what it claims to be and is free of unauthorized alteration
formal act of taking legal and physical custody of records and recording it
an addition of records to an existing fonds or collection
instrument mapping record series to retention periods and disposition actions
final action on records: transfer to archives, destruction, or migration
descriptive tool (e.g., DACS/EAD) providing access to archival materials

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established archival science and records-management literature (Schellenberg; Cook macro-appraisal; Upward records continuum; DACS/EAD/ISAD(G)/RiC standards; Rubin & Rubin 2020; Johnston 2017) and professional practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Select and document the governing appraisal theory (Schellenberg values, macro-appraisal, documentation strategy) before any retain/destroy decision.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when institutional mandate, collecting scope, or functional structure materially changes

pros.claim: separating theory from case-by-case judgment makes retain/destroy decisions reproducible and auditable
pros.example: macro-appraisal anchors selection to documented functions, not appraiser taste

cons.claim: a single theory can misfit hybrid holdings, forcing later re-appraisal
cons.example: function-based macro-appraisal underweights serendipitous informational value in personal papers

failure_modes: theory chosen post-hoc to justify a decision already made
value criteria left undefined so appraisers diverge
acceptance_tests: appraisal theory and value criteria documented before any disposition decision
each disposition decision cites a defined value criterion
revisit_triggers: new accession class outside current theory fit
audit finding of inconsistent value application

nodes.definition: Apply the chosen value criteria to a records body and record a justified, reviewable retain/sample/destroy recommendation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reappraisal, deaccession review, or new evidential value claims arise

pros.claim: a written appraisal report makes destruction defensible and reversible-in-reasoning even when records are not
pros.example: a report citing low secondary value justifies sampling routine vouchers

cons.claim: destruction acting on a wrong appraisal is irreversible and high-liability
cons.example: destroying records later found to have legal evidential value

failure_modes: destruction executed before report review
sampling plan not representative of the series
acceptance_tests: appraisal report peer-reviewed before any destruction
disposition recommendation maps each criterion to a decision
irreversible destruction gated on human review

nodes.definition: Establish and preserve the records' creator-based provenance (respect des fonds), grouping records by origin rather than subject.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a records body is found to mix creators or custodial history is revised

pros.claim: provenance keeps the evidential context that gives records their meaning and authenticity
pros.example: keeping a department's files together preserves the function that produced them

cons.claim: rigid fonds boundaries can fragment cross-creator activities users expect together
cons.example: a joint project's records split across two fonds frustrate discovery

failure_modes: records re-filed by subject, destroying creator context
fonds boundary drawn around format not creator
acceptance_tests: fonds boundaries documented with creator and custodial history
no records regrouped by subject across creators

nodes.definition: Determine, preserve, or reconstruct the order in which the creator kept the records, deviating only with documented justification.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when received order is found disturbed or a better-evidenced original order emerges

pros.claim: original order reveals the creator's own logic and usage, an evidential asset
pros.example: a chronological case-file order shows workflow that resorting would erase

cons.claim: a badly disturbed order may be unusable, forcing a documented imposed order
cons.example: papers dumped in boxes have no recoverable original order

failure_modes: order resorted for tidiness without justification
imposed order applied without documenting it
acceptance_tests: any deviation from received order documented with rationale
series scheme traces to creator logic where recoverable
revisit_triggers: evidence original order was disturbed in custody
user complaints that imposed order obscures use

nodes.definition: Organize materials into the multilevel hierarchy (repository, fonds, series, file, item) that expresses provenance and order.

excluded: storage location assignment beyond intellectual order

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when accruals extend a series or a new level of arrangement becomes necessary

pros.claim: multilevel arrangement lets description be done once at the right level, scaling to large fonds
pros.example: series-level processing handles 200 boxes without item listing

cons.claim: choosing too granular a level inflates processing cost without user benefit
cons.example: item-listing routine correspondence wastes processing time

failure_modes: arrangement level chosen by habit not by content
intellectual and physical arrangement conflated
revisit_triggers: large new accrual to an existing series
processing backlog pressure forcing level change

nodes.definition: Produce content-standard-compliant multilevel description (DACS) capturing required elements at each level of arrangement.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when DACS revises required elements or a new level is added

pros.claim: content standards make finding aids interoperable and reviewable for completeness
pros.example: DACS single-level minimum guarantees a usable record even for unprocessed accessions

cons.claim: standard compliance can encourage box-checking over meaningful scope notes
cons.example: complete element set with an uninformative scope-and-content note

failure_modes: required elements omitted at a level
description authored before arrangement is stable

nodes.definition: Encode finding aids in EAD (XML) so descriptions are machine-actionable, harvestable, and standards-validated.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when EAD schema version changes or discovery platform requirements shift

pros.claim: EAD makes finding aids harvestable and validatable, enabling aggregation and reuse
pros.example: valid EAD3 feeds a consortial portal automatically

cons.claim: encoding before description is final causes rework on every content edit
cons.example: re-tagging XML after scope notes are rewritten

failure_modes: EAD encoded against unstable description
invalid XML shipped to discovery system

nodes.definition: Map description to ISAD(G) general international standard to support cross-repository and international exchange.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an international exchange partner or aggregator requires ISAD(G) conformance

pros.claim: ISAD(G) alignment enables cross-border discovery and aggregation
pros.example: a crosswalk lets European partners ingest the finding aid

cons.claim: element mismatches between content standards cause lossy crosswalks
cons.example: DACS statement of responsibility has no clean ISAD(G) home

failure_modes: lossy crosswalk silently drops elements
crosswalk maintained as a one-off, not repeatable

nodes.definition: Model description as a graph using Records in Contexts (RiC) to represent multiple provenance and complex agent-record relationships.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when holdings exhibit multiple or shifting provenance that hierarchy cannot express

pros.claim: RiC expresses multiple provenance and agent relationships hierarchy forces into a single tree
pros.example: records reassigned between agencies are modeled as relations, not duplicated

cons.claim: graph modeling raises complexity and tooling cost over established hierarchical practice
cons.example: staff trained on EAD must learn ontologies and triple stores

failure_modes: RiC adopted without staff capacity, producing inconsistent graphs
graph diverges from authoritative hierarchical description
revisit_triggers: discovery of multiprovenance requiring graph model

nodes.definition: Take physical and legal custody of incoming records, recording extent, source, and rights, and assigning a unique accession identifier.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when rights, extent, or source information for an accession is corrected

pros.claim: a complete accession record establishes legal custody and a baseline for all later control
pros.example: recorded deed of gift settles future rights questions

cons.claim: rushed accessioning omits rights/extent data that is costly to recover later
cons.example: missing deed of gift blocks later digitization rights

failure_modes: custody taken without documented rights
accession number not assigned, breaking control
acceptance_tests: every accession has a unique control number and rights statement
extent recorded at accession

nodes.definition: Manage anticipated and unanticipated additions to existing fonds so arrangement, description, and identifiers integrate consistently.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an unanticipated accrual disrupts an existing series or identifier scheme

pros.claim: planning for accruals keeps open fonds coherent over time
pros.example: reserved series numbers absorb annual transfers cleanly

cons.claim: treating fonds as closed forces re-arrangement when accruals arrive
cons.example: a finalized finding aid must be reworked for an unexpected transfer

failure_modes: accrual filed as a new fonds, fragmenting provenance
identifier collisions on integration

nodes.definition: Define and maintain records retention schedules linking record series to retention periods and final disposition actions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when laws, regulations, or business rules governing retention change

pros.claim: schedules turn appraisal into repeatable, defensible lifecycle actions
pros.example: a cited statutory period authorizes routine destruction of expired records

cons.claim: a wrong or stale schedule can authorize destruction of still-valuable records
cons.example: an outdated period triggers destruction before a litigation hold

failure_modes: schedule applied without legal review
disposition triggered while a hold is active
acceptance_tests: retention periods cite a legal/regulatory authority
schedule reviewed before disposition triggers fire

nodes.definition: Execute final disposition (transfer to archives, destruction, or migration) per the schedule, with verified, documented, irreversible action control.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a hold, audit, or legal challenge contests a pending or executed disposition

pros.claim: verified disposition with a certificate makes destruction auditable and compliant
pros.example: a signed destruction certificate evidences lawful, scheduled destruction

cons.claim: destruction is irreversible; any error or missed hold is unrecoverable
cons.example: automated deletion ignores an unrecorded litigation hold

failure_modes: destruction proceeds despite an active hold
no certificate produced, breaking the audit trail
acceptance_tests: active-hold check passes before any destruction
disposition certificate produced for every action
human review before irreversible destruction

nodes.definition: Choose and apply the governing records model (linear lifecycle vs records continuum) shaping when appraisal and capture intervene.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when born-digital systems require appraisal at creation rather than at transfer

pros.claim: the continuum model lets appraisal intervene at creation, vital for born-digital records
pros.example: capture-point appraisal preserves email before it is deleted by users

cons.claim: forcing a linear lifecycle on continuous digital systems delays appraisal until records are lost
cons.example: waiting for transfer loses ephemeral cloud records

failure_modes: model chosen by tradition, mismatching the records environment
appraisal deferred past the point records survive
revisit_triggers: adoption of new born-digital creation systems
evidence records are lost before transfer

nodes.definition: Establish and maintain records' authenticity, reliability, and integrity so they can be trusted as evidence over time.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a fixity check fails or a record's provenance/integrity is challenged

pros.claim: documented authenticity lets records stand as legal and historical evidence
pros.example: checksums plus custody history rebut a tampering claim

cons.claim: authenticity controls add overhead and can be skipped under throughput pressure
cons.example: fixity baselining skipped during a large rushed ingest

failure_modes: integrity baseline never captured at ingest
authenticity asserted without supporting metadata
acceptance_tests: integrity baseline (checksums) captured at accession
authenticity assessment documents identity and integrity evidence

nodes.definition: Maintain an unbroken, documented chain of custody recording every transfer and action affecting records since creation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a custody gap is discovered or a new transfer must be logged

pros.claim: an unbroken custody record underpins authenticity and admissibility
pros.example: a complete log shows no opportunity for undocumented alteration

cons.claim: custody gaps before acquisition may be unrecoverable, weakening evidential weight
cons.example: records donated decades after creation have undocumented intervening custody

failure_modes: custody events logged inconsistently or retroactively
gap left undocumented, hiding a trust weakness
acceptance_tests: each custody transfer logged with date, agent, and action
custody gaps documented rather than concealed
revisit_triggers: discovery of an undocumented custody gap

nodes.definition: Appraise born-digital and electronic records accounting for format, volume, system dependency, and capture timing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new file formats, volumes, or creation systems exceed current appraisal methods

pros.claim: digital-aware appraisal captures fragile born-digital evidence before it is lost
pros.example: forensic disk imaging preserves deleted-but-recoverable context

cons.claim: over-capturing everything digital defers the appraisal burden and inflates storage risk
cons.example: imaging every drive without appraisal creates an unmanageable dark archive

failure_modes: appraisal deferred until records are unreadable
capture method ignores system dependencies
acceptance_tests: capture method documented per accession with format risk
appraisal applied before bulk ingest, not after
human review for high-risk digital destruction
revisit_triggers: obsolescence warning for a held format

nodes.definition: Determine and document access conditions, restrictions, and privacy protections governing use of the records.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when privacy law changes or an embargo period expires

pros.claim: documented restrictions balance access with legal and privacy obligations
pros.example: a timed embargo opens records automatically while protecting living individuals

cons.claim: over-restriction needlessly blocks access; under-restriction breaches privacy
cons.example: releasing PII-laden case files breaches data-protection law

failure_modes: PII released without screening
blanket closure applied without legal basis
acceptance_tests: PII/privacy screening completed before access is opened
each restriction cites a legal or donor basis
human review before releasing sensitive series

nodes.definition: Publish finding aids and access systems that deliver description and enforce access conditions to users.
inputs: valid EAD XML / finding aid content

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when access policy or discovery platform requirements change

pros.claim: publishing finding aids turns hidden processing into actual user access
pros.example: a loaded finding aid lets researchers find a series without staff mediation

cons.claim: delivery that does not enforce restrictions can expose closed material
cons.example: a public finding aid leaks a restricted file's existence and contents

failure_modes: restricted content surfaced in public discovery
finding aid published before restrictions are set

nodes.definition: Enable description to be exchanged, harvested, and aggregated across repositories and portals via shared standards and identifiers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an aggregator changes its conformance profile or identifier requirements

pros.claim: aggregation multiplies discovery reach with one well-formed export
pros.example: a single harvest feeds a national archival portal

cons.claim: aggregator-specific profiles fragment effort and break on upstream changes
cons.example: a portal profile change silently invalidates the harvest feed

failure_modes: exports drift out of conformance unnoticed
identifiers not persistent, breaking aggregated links

nodes.definition: Govern the appraisal/description program with policy, peer review, and quality assurance so decisions are consistent, documented, and auditable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when audit reveals inconsistent appraisal or description across the program

pros.claim: program QA catches inconsistent value application before it becomes systemic
pros.example: peer review flags an appraiser destroying a series others would keep

cons.claim: heavy review can bottleneck throughput if not risk-tiered
cons.example: every routine disposition queued for full peer review stalls operations

failure_modes: QA applied only after disposition, too late to prevent loss
review not risk-tiered, creating bottlenecks

edges.why_related: theory and value criteria define how decisions are made
edges.risk_of_conflict: deciding without a theory yields arbitrary results
edges.example: macro-appraisal frames which functions to keep

edges.why_related: the appraisal theory shapes when intervention occurs
edges.risk_of_conflict: model chosen without theory misfits intervention points
edges.example: function-based theory favors capture-point continuum

edges.why_related: the records model sets when digital records are appraised
edges.risk_of_conflict: late model choice loses ephemeral records
edges.example: continuum triggers email capture at creation

edges.why_related: value criteria govern digital selection too
edges.risk_of_conflict: digital appraised by different rules than analog
edges.example: same secondary-value test applied to email
edges.resolution_rule: apply one value framework across media

edges.why_related: appraisal outcomes populate retention periods and disposition
edges.risk_of_conflict: scheduling without appraisal sets arbitrary periods
edges.example: a low-value series gets a short retention

edges.why_related: the approved schedule authorizes disposition actions
edges.risk_of_conflict: disposition without a schedule is unlawful
edges.example: an expired period triggers scheduled destruction
edges.resolution_rule: never dispose without an approved, hold-checked schedule

edges.why_related: the appraisal report justifies the disposition action
edges.risk_of_conflict: disposing without a report breaks the audit trail
edges.example: the report evidences why a series is destroyed
edges.resolution_rule: require the appraisal report before disposition

edges.why_related: creator identity frames what original order means
edges.benefit_of_coupling: order is read against the right creator
edges.risk_of_conflict: ordering before provenance mixes creators
edges.example: series order interpreted within the fonds

edges.why_related: fonds boundaries drive the arrangement hierarchy
edges.risk_of_conflict: arranging before provenance fragments context
edges.example: fonds defines the top arrangement level

edges.why_related: the order decision determines series sequencing
edges.risk_of_conflict: arranging before the order decision risks resorting
edges.example: series follow the documented order
edges.resolution_rule: decide order before building the hierarchy

edges.why_related: arrangement levels define what is described at each level
edges.risk_of_conflict: describing before arrangement causes rework
edges.example: series-level scope notes follow series grouping

edges.why_related: provenance supplies creator and custodial description elements
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing provenance yields contextless records
edges.example: creator and custodial history populate DACS

edges.why_related: stable description content is what gets encoded
edges.benefit_of_coupling: encoding is done once on final content
edges.risk_of_conflict: encoding unstable content causes re-tagging
edges.example: scope notes become EAD elements

edges.why_related: DACS content is the source for ISAD(G) mapping
edges.risk_of_conflict: crosswalking unstable content multiplies edits
edges.example: DACS elements map to ISAD(G) fields

edges.why_related: provenance entities are RiC's modeling primitives
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling without provenance yields wrong relations
edges.example: creators become RiC agent entities

edges.why_related: descriptive content seeds RiC entities and relations
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling diverges from authoritative description
edges.example: scope notes inform RiC relations
edges.resolution_rule: keep RiC consistent with DACS content

edges.why_related: valid EAD is the harvestable artifact for aggregation
edges.risk_of_conflict: exchanging invalid EAD breaks harvests
edges.example: valid EAD3 feeds a portal

edges.why_related: ISAD(G) alignment enables international exchange
edges.risk_of_conflict: unaligned description fails partner ingest
edges.example: ISAD(G) export ingested by a partner

edges.why_related: RiC linked-data export feeds graph aggregators
edges.risk_of_conflict: ungoverned graphs fragment aggregation
edges.example: RiC-O export joins a knowledge graph
edges.resolution_rule: govern RiC before publishing for exchange

edges.why_related: accession control is the baseline for appraising a body
edges.benefit_of_coupling: appraisal acts on a controlled accession
edges.risk_of_conflict: appraising un-accessioned records loses control
edges.example: the accession record scopes what is appraised

edges.why_related: accession extent and structure inform arrangement
edges.risk_of_conflict: arranging un-accessioned records is uncontrolled
edges.example: extent guides the arrangement plan

edges.why_related: the initial accession defines what accruals extend
edges.benefit_of_coupling: accruals integrate into a known fonds
edges.risk_of_conflict: accruals without a base accession fragment fonds
edges.example: an accrual joins the original accession's fonds

edges.why_related: the arrangement scheme is what accruals must fit
edges.risk_of_conflict: accruals to an unplanned scheme force re-arrangement
edges.example: reserved series absorb the accrual

edges.why_related: accession is when integrity baselines are captured
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping baseline at intake loses integrity proof
edges.example: checksums taken at accession

edges.why_related: authenticity depends on documented custody
edges.risk_of_conflict: authenticity claims without custody are weak
edges.example: custody log corroborates integrity

edges.why_related: accession transfer is the first custody event
edges.risk_of_conflict: unrecorded intake breaks the chain
edges.example: intake logged as a custody event

edges.why_related: digital appraisal must preserve integrity evidence
edges.risk_of_conflict: capture that ignores integrity destroys evidence
edges.example: disk image preserves fixity and context

edges.why_related: deed terms captured at accession govern access
edges.risk_of_conflict: restrictions set without terms are baseless
edges.example: a donor embargo recorded at accession

edges.why_related: appraisal surfaces sensitive content needing restriction
edges.risk_of_conflict: unappraised content hides PII risk
edges.example: appraisal flags case files with PII

edges.why_related: published description is what access tools deliver
edges.risk_of_conflict: publishing without description gives nothing to find
edges.example: a finding aid is loaded for search

edges.why_related: access tools must enforce the restriction policy
edges.risk_of_conflict: tools without restriction logic leak closed material
edges.example: restricted files hidden in discovery

edges.why_related: schedules feed program-level QA and audit
edges.risk_of_conflict: unreviewed schedules drift
edges.example: QA audits schedule citations

edges.why_related: QA review of reports can trigger reappraisal
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded re-review stalls work
edges.example: peer review returns a flawed report
edges.resolution_rule: stop when reports meet QA criteria; cap re-review per cycle

edges.why_related: description QA can send finding aids back for fixes
edges.risk_of_conflict: endless QA loops block release
edges.example: QA flags missing required elements
edges.resolution_rule: stop when DACS required elements pass; cap revision rounds

edges.why_related: the records model bounds when scheduling intervenes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scheduling fits the model's intervention points
edges.risk_of_conflict: model-schedule mismatch delays disposition
edges.example: continuum schedules act at creation
edges.resolution_rule: align schedule timing to the chosen model

edges.why_related: local descriptive richness tensions with exchange simplicity
edges.risk_of_conflict: forcing exchange formats drops local detail
edges.example: rich DACS notes flatten in aggregator export
edges.resolution_rule: local detail dominates when mandated; otherwise prefer exchange profile and note loss

edges.why_related: broad appraisal/keeping tensions with timely access delivery
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-keeping delays processing and access
edges.example: large unappraised backlog blocks publication
edges.resolution_rule: access throughput yields to correct appraisal; use MPLP minimal processing to relieve tension

edges.why_related: privacy restriction tensions with open access delivery
edges.risk_of_conflict: opening too much breaches privacy; closing too much blocks use
edges.example: a PII series demands closure users want open
edges.resolution_rule: privacy/legal restriction dominates over openness; document basis and set timed release

edges.why_related: preserving original order tensions with user-friendly access ordering
edges.risk_of_conflict: resorting for usability destroys evidential order
edges.example: users want chronological but order is by function
edges.resolution_rule: original order dominates; provide access indexes rather than resorting

edges.why_related: aggressive digital culling tensions with irreversible disposition risk
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balances volume control against loss risk
edges.risk_of_conflict: deleting digital records prematurely is irreversible
edges.example: bulk-deleting to save storage loses evidence
edges.resolution_rule: irreversibility dominates: require review before digital destruction; prefer staged, reversible holds

conflict_axes.trigger: appraisal must choose between keeping marginal records and authorizing irreversible destruction
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: irreversibility dominates: when in doubt and value is plausible, retain or sample rather than destroy
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if value is contested and destruction is proposed
conflict_axes.example: APPRAISAL_DECISION peer-reviewed and held series kept

conflict_axes.trigger: users want subject/chronological access while provenance and original order must be preserved
resolution_order: add access indexes and finding-aid navigation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: provenance and original order dominate; serve usability through indexes, not by resorting records
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if staff propose resorting records for usability
conflict_axes.example: original order kept; access index added

conflict_axes.trigger: local descriptive depth can be lost in exchange/aggregation profiles
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: mandated local detail dominates; otherwise adopt the exchange profile and record the loss
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no exchange profile preserves a mandated element
conflict_axes.example: local record kept authoritative; loss noted

conflict_axes.trigger: openness goals collide with privacy, donor, and legal restrictions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: privacy and legal restriction dominate access openness; document basis and minimize closure scope
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if sensitive content would be exposed by opening access

conflict_axes.trigger: deep arrangement/description competes with clearing backlog for access
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for low-risk high-volume holdings throughput dominates via minimal processing; high-value gets depth
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if backlog blocks access to high-demand collections

conflict_axes.trigger: linear lifecycle defers appraisal while continuum demands capture-point appraisal for digital
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for volatile born-digital records the continuum model dominates to avoid loss before transfer
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if born-digital records are lost before transfer

conflict_axes.trigger: automated schedule-driven disposition competes with human review of irreversible actions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: human review dominates for irreversible or high-risk disposition; automation only for vetted low-risk
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if automated deletion could act despite a hold
conflict_axes.example: human review gate enforced before destruction

conflict_axes.trigger: capturing integrity/custody evidence competes with high-volume digital throughput
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: integrity and custody capture dominate at ingest; volume managed by staging, not by skipping baselines
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if throughput pressure tempts skipping fixity baselines

conflict_axes.trigger: established hierarchical standards compete with RiC graph modeling for effort and tooling
resolution_order: adopt RiC where graph value is clear
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: hierarchical standards dominate by default; RiC adopted only where multiprovenance value exceeds cost
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if RiC is proposed without staff capacity or clear need

edge_cases.trigger: destruction executed before the appraisal report is peer-reviewed
edge_cases.failure_mode: irreversible loss of records later found valuable
edge_cases.example: a series destroyed the same day its report was drafted, before review
edge_cases.detection_method: log shows disposition action timestamp earlier than report review approval
resolution: block disposition until report is approved
require human review for irreversible destruction

edge_cases.trigger: scheduled disposition fires while a legal hold is active
edge_cases.failure_mode: spoliation: destruction of records under legal hold
edge_cases.example: an expired-period series under litigation hold queued for destruction
edge_cases.detection_method: cross-check disposition queue against active-hold register before execution
resolution: enforce active-hold gate before any disposition

edge_cases.trigger: records from multiple creators filed as one fonds
edge_cases.failure_mode: false provenance corrupting evidential context and authenticity
edge_cases.example: two agencies' files merged under one fonds during a rushed transfer
edge_cases.detection_method: audit creator attribution against accession and custodial records
resolution: split mixed records into correct fonds

edge_cases.trigger: original order resorted for tidiness without documented justification
edge_cases.failure_mode: loss of evidential order revealing creator workflow
edge_cases.example: case files re-alphabetized, erasing a meaningful chronological workflow
edge_cases.detection_method: compare arrangement to received order; require a deviation justification record
resolution: record any imposed order with rationale

edge_cases.trigger: description/encoding done before arrangement is stable
edge_cases.failure_mode: rework across description and EAD on every arrangement change
edge_cases.example: EAD re-tagged repeatedly because series boundaries kept changing
edge_cases.detection_method: check that arrangement is soft-locked before description begins

edge_cases.trigger: finding aid or system exposes restricted PII content
edge_cases.example: a public finding aid revealed names in a closed medical case series
edge_cases.detection_method: automated PII/sensitivity scan of published description and access display before release

edge_cases.trigger: crosswalk silently drops mandated descriptive elements
edge_cases.example: statement-of-responsibility data lost when mapping DACS to an exchange profile
edge_cases.detection_method: round-trip crosswalk test comparing source elements to exported elements

edge_cases.trigger: digital records ingested without an integrity baseline
edge_cases.failure_mode: inability to prove integrity or detect later corruption
edge_cases.example: a large drive ingested under deadline with no checksums captured
edge_cases.detection_method: verify checksums exist for every digital accession at intake

edge_cases.failure_mode: weakened evidential weight and authenticity claims
edge_cases.example: decades between creation and donation with no intervening custody recorded
edge_cases.detection_method: audit custody log for unexplained time gaps between events

edge_cases.trigger: born-digital appraisal deferred until records are unreadable or deleted
edge_cases.failure_mode: permanent loss of ephemeral born-digital records
edge_cases.example: cloud collaboration records auto-purged before any appraisal occurred
edge_cases.detection_method: monitor format obsolescence and creation-system retention against appraisal timing

edge_cases.trigger: a computed score diverges from its formula or an evidence label is wrong
edge_cases.example: final_importance hand-edited and no longer matches the weighted formula
edge_cases.detection_method: run kb_validator formula.consistency and evidence-label checks

edge_cases.trigger: a dependent node ordered before its unmet prerequisite
edge_cases.failure_mode: rework when downstream work is finalized before upstream is stable
edge_cases.example: description prioritized ahead of the arrangement it depends on
edge_cases.detection_method: check priority_order against dependency edges for inversions
resolution: mark draft-only where early start is intentional

workflow.objective: fix the governing appraisal theory, value criteria, and records model before any decision
acceptance_tests: theory and criteria documented before any disposition
model fits the records environment
workflow.do_first_because: theory, criteria, and model are the highest-coupling foundations all later steps depend on

workflow.objective: take controlled custody and establish authenticity and chain-of-custody baselines
acceptance_tests: every accession has a control number and rights statement
integrity baseline captured at intake
workflow.do_first_because: custody, rights, and integrity must be fixed at intake or they are unrecoverable later

workflow.objective: apply value criteria to accessioned records and author reviewable appraisal reports
acceptance_tests: each decision cites a defined value criterion
report peer-reviewed before any destruction
workflow.do_first_because: appraisal must precede scheduling and disposition to keep destruction defensible

workflow.objective: translate appraisal outcomes into legally-cited retention periods and disposition triggers
acceptance_tests: each retention period cites a legal authority
schedule reviewed before triggers fire
workflow.do_first_because: a cited, approved schedule must exist before any disposition is authorized

workflow.objective: determine fonds boundaries and original order before arranging
acceptance_tests: fonds boundaries documented with creator and custodial history
order deviations justified
workflow.do_first_because: provenance and order frame all arrangement and description; fixing them early prevents re-arrangement

workflow.objective: build the multilevel arrangement hierarchy and plan for accruals
acceptance_tests: arrangement level justified by content
accrual scheme reserves capacity
workflow.do_first_because: a stable arrangement is required before description to avoid description rework

workflow.objective: author DACS-compliant multilevel description on the stable arrangement
acceptance_tests: required DACS elements present at each level
scope notes informative
workflow.do_first_because: describing only after arrangement is stable prevents repeated rework

workflow.objective: encode finding aids (EAD), crosswalk to ISAD(G), and model RiC where multiprovenance warrants
acceptance_tests: EAD validates against schema
crosswalk round-trip loses no mandated element
workflow.do_first_because: encode only finalized description to avoid re-tagging on every content edit

workflow.objective: determine restrictions, publish access tools that enforce them, and enable aggregation
acceptance_tests: PII screened before opening access
access display enforces restrictions
workflow.do_first_because: restrictions must be set and enforced before any access delivery to prevent privacy breaches

workflow.objective: execute hold-checked, documented disposition for records reaching end of retention
acceptance_tests: no active hold before destruction
disposition certificate produced
human review for irreversible destruction
workflow.do_first_because: disposition is irreversible and must run last, only after schedule, holds, and review gates pass

workflow.objective: run program QA, peer review, and audit across appraisal and description outputs
entry_criteria: appraisal reports and finding aids produced
acceptance_tests: high-risk decisions peer-reviewed
decision records complete and auditable
workflow.do_first_because: program governance runs continuously to catch inconsistency before it becomes systemic loss

dominance_rules.trigger: a faster appraisal/disposition path risks correctness or irreversible loss
dominance_rules.rule: never accept a speed gain that risks destroying valuable or held records
dominance_rules.required_action: block disposition until appraisal review and hold checks pass
dominance_rules.example: destroying a series faster but before peer review of its appraisal report

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is ready but its prerequisite is not finalized
dominance_rules.rule: do not finalize a node before its dependencies are reviewed
dominance_rules.required_action: reorder execution to respect dependency edges and priority_order
dominance_rules.example: encoding EAD before the description it depends on is approved

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible action (destruction) is proposed for convenience
dominance_rules.rule: irreversible actions require human review and verified holds first
dominance_rules.required_action: require human_review_required and active-hold gate before destruction
dominance_rules.example: auto-deleting expired digital records to free storage

dominance_rules.trigger: opening access would expose restricted or private content
dominance_rules.rule: privacy and legal restrictions dominate openness; minimize but enforce closure
dominance_rules.required_action: screen for PII and enforce restrictions in delivery before publishing
dominance_rules.example: publishing a finding aid that exposes a closed medical series

dominance_rules.trigger: resorting records would improve usability but break original order
dominance_rules.rule: preserve provenance and original order; serve usability via indexes not resorting
dominance_rules.required_action: add access indexes; document any necessary imposed order
dominance_rules.example: alphabetizing case files that have a meaningful chronological order

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise-looking score lacks eligible evidence
dominance_rules.rule: evidence-label correctness dominates apparent numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels; set observed/experimental fields to 0.0 without data
dominance_rules.example: labeling a heuristic risk estimate as observed to look authoritative

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact is ready to lock but has not passed QA
dominance_rules.rule: QA must pass before soft or hard lock
dominance_rules.required_action: block lock until GOVERNANCE_QA and validation checks pass
dominance_rules.example: hard-locking a finding aid that failed required-element QA

dominance_rules.trigger: an automated decision crosses a risk or irreversibility threshold
dominance_rules.rule: human review overrides automation above risk/irreversibility thresholds
dominance_rules.required_action: route high-risk or irreversible actions to a human reviewer
dominance_rules.example: automated disposition acting on a series with contested value

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim exceeds what the source registry supports
dominance_rules.rule: claims must not exceed eligible source support
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade to heuristic or reference SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR; remove overclaim
dominance_rules.example: asserting measured interoperability rates with only heuristic priors

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient sequencing would create a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.rule: keep dependency edges acyclic even if a cycle would be convenient
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker dependency to sequence/feedback and add a revisit rule
dominance_rules.example: making appraisal depend on disposition to shortcut scheduling

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix appraisal theory and value criteria before any retain/destroy decision
anti_rework_rules.rationale: decisions made without a theory are arbitrary and get re-litigated
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a disposition decision exists with no cited value criterion
anti_rework_rules.example: destroying a series, then drafting a theory to justify it

anti_rework_rules.rule: accession and capture custody/integrity before appraisal, arrangement, or description
anti_rework_rules.rationale: processing un-accessioned records loses control and integrity proof
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: processing work begins with no accession record
anti_rework_rules.example: arranging records before a control number or rights statement exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish provenance and original order before arrangement
anti_rework_rules.rationale: arranging before provenance fragments creator context and forces re-arrangement
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an arrangement hierarchy exists before fonds boundaries are set
anti_rework_rules.example: building a hierarchy that later splits one creator across fonds

anti_rework_rules.rationale: describing an unstable arrangement causes description rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: scope notes authored while series boundaries still change
anti_rework_rules.example: writing series-level notes before series are finalized

anti_rework_rules.rule: finalize description content before EAD encoding and crosswalks
anti_rework_rules.rationale: encoding unstable content forces re-tagging on every edit
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: EAD or crosswalk produced before description is approved
anti_rework_rules.example: re-encoding XML after every scope-note revision

anti_rework_rules.rule: appraise before authoring retention schedules and before disposition
anti_rework_rules.rationale: scheduling or disposing without appraisal sets arbitrary, indefensible actions
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a retention period exists with no appraisal basis
anti_rework_rules.example: assigning a retention period before any value assessment

anti_rework_rules.rule: determine and configure access restrictions before publishing access tools
anti_rework_rules.rationale: publishing before restrictions are set risks exposing closed material
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an access tool is published before restrictions are configured
anti_rework_rules.example: loading a finding aid that surfaces an unscreened PII series

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify legal holds and human review before any irreversible disposition
blocked_until: human review completed for irreversible action
anti_rework_rules.rationale: destruction under a hold is spoliation and unrecoverable
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a disposition action lacks a hold-verification record
anti_rework_rules.example: destroying an expired series that is under litigation hold

anti_rework_rules.rule: capture integrity baselines and custody before locking digital ingest
anti_rework_rules.rationale: without a baseline, later corruption cannot be proven or detected
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a digital accession is finalized with no checksums
anti_rework_rules.example: locking an ingest under deadline with no fixity captured

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or QA flags a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report and QA deltas to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk_score and irreversibility
action: score defects by risk and irreversibility
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect addressed first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only low-risk defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a locked or high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependency and edge impact from the defect node
acceptance_tests: all downstream dependents identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across two passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to a repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: repair applied by the correct subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run kb_validator and recompute derived scores
acceptance_tests: formula.consistency passes
no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a materiality-crossing change occurs
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed for affected nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changed after dependents were locked
iteration_protocol.detection: downgrade affected locks and re-open for review
acceptance_tests: all affected dependents downgraded
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no locked dependent has a changed upstream

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk or irreversibility crosses a human-review threshold
iteration_protocol.detection: check risk_score and irreversibility against thresholds
acceptance_tests: high-risk/irreversible items reviewed by a human

checks.repair_action: converted weaker dependency to sequence/feedback where needed
recomputed all derived scores from formulas

change_triggers: adoption of new born-digital creation systems
version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked artifact change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
downgrade arrangement-dependent description on arrangement change
human_approval_required_for: disposition under any prior or active hold
